name: Shiva hippocampus signal (normal speed)
origin: Shiva software by Todd Murphy (signal templates licensed from Persinger and Koren)
summary: Murphy's simple Shiva session: the hippocampal 'LTP' theta-burst signal stepped counter-clockwise around the head at normal speed. The vendor presents it for cognitive, non-verbal, imagery and intuition effects.
notes: Coils sit on Murphy's Shiva ring (Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2; one coil per site instead of Shiva's coil pairs) and step counter-clockwise seen from above, with Murphy's lecture example of 10, 12 ... 20 ms per coil (about 8 rotations a second; Murphy writes 'around 9 times per second'). Phase 1 (20 min) is the 20-min version; phase 2 makes it the 30-min version (a 60-min Shiva version also exists). The Shiva LTP file is proprietary. It is approximated by a point table in Murphy's standard scheme (3-ms points, about 4 s of latency): a train of 4 theta bursts, each of 4 biphasic pulses 9 ms apart (after the 4-pulse 100 Hz bursts of Larson & Lynch), repeated every 186 ms (5.4 Hz, the spectral peak the vendor reports for its LTP signal), then 4 s of silence, so the trains fill about 9.4 s of each minute (the vendor gives 'approximately 9.6 seconds exposure' per minute). Shiva also has a 'slow' version, found by accident in 1998 and not used in formal studies; its parameters are unpublished, so it is not included. Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994 used 1 µT LTP-pattern fields for 20 min. Murphy's cautions: word-finding problems or feeling 'spaced out' mean switch to another signal; about 2% get headaches or pressure, in which case lower the intensity by one-third. Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy; stop if distressed.
setting: Dark, quiet room, eyes closed, relaxed without meditating or falling asleep. Shiva offers 20, 30 and 60-min versions; start with the short one.
schedule: At most once a week, never on consecutive days; up to 6 sessions, then a 21-day break. 60-min sessions weekly or every two weeks at most.
